card.summary: 'Nebula is a scalable overlay networking tool with a focus on performance, simplicity and security. It lets you seamlessly connect computers anywhere in the ...

free_tier.stated: 'Nebula is a scalable overlay networking tool with a focus on performance, simplicity and security. It lets you seamlessly connect computers anywhere in the network.' Self-hosted; no quota.

egress.terms: No allowance: there is no vendor and no hosted service.; ingress: none

record.interface_detail: config files plus a certificate authority the operator runs
record.chaining: a private overlay that composes with a public ingress and adds none
record.binding_note: Nothing meters bytes and nothing publishes a port, so no constraint fires at 1 TiB/month because the traffic cannot leave the overlay.

identity_cost.detail: self-hosted; membership is a signed certificate from the operator's CA

record.reliability_note: self-operated; certificate issuance and lighthouse uptime are local work
record.confidence_note: The overlay claim is quoted; the 'no ingress' conclusion is inferred from the description, because a feature that does not exist has no page saying so. Reading the lighthouse documentation would raise this to documented.

evidence.proved: 'Nebula is a scalable overlay networking tool'; it 'lets you seamlessly connect computers anywhere in the network' and combines 'encryption, security groups, certificates, and tunneling'

record.notes: Included because the supplied list names it and because a reader will confuse it with a WireGuard tool.

extras.wg_detail: The repository describes 'encryption, security groups, certificates, and tunneling' without naming WireGuard; no protocol page was read, so whether the transport can carry a WireGuard datagram is open.
extras.volume_stated: No allowance: there is no vendor and no hosted service.
extras.transit_note: peers relay through lighthouses only to find each other; payload goes peer to peer
